# Model and source

Thai 2023 developed a joint model of serum M-protein kinetics and
progression-free survival (PFS) for single-agent isatuximab, with or without
dexamethasone, in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM). It used the
model to simulate the 10 and 20 mg/kg weekly-then-biweekly (qw-q2w) regimens,
with and without dexamethasone, in Japanese patients, and so supported the
Japanese approval of isatuximab +/- dexamethasone without an extra trial.

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Thai_2023_isatuximab"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.12947> (open access; Appendix S1 holds
  the Monolix model code).

The model has four layers, all in one file because the authors fitted the
M-protein and PFS parts jointly:

1. **Isatuximab PK.** The Fau 2020 two-compartment model with parallel
   time-varying linear and Michaelis-Menten elimination (also available on its
   own as `modellib("Fau_2020_isatuximab")`). Thai 2023 used individual
   post-hoc PK parameters from it; here its population parameters and
   between-subject variability are embedded as fixed values, converted from
   hours to days.
2. **Dexamethasone K-PD.** Dexamethasone concentrations were not measured, so
   doses enter a virtual compartment with a fixed elimination rate constant
   (2.42 /day) and volume (76.3 L).
3. **Serum M-protein.** A Claret tumor-growth-inhibition model:

   $$\frac{dM}{dt} = K_L M - K_D e^{-R t}\left(\frac{C_{iM}}{EC_{50} + C_{iM}} + k\,C_{dM}\right) M, \quad M(0) = M_0$$

   where $C_{iM}$ and $C_{dM}$ are the isatuximab and dexamethasone molar
   concentrations (umol/L).
4. **PFS.** A log-logistic baseline hazard multiplied by baseline covariates
   and by the instantaneous M-protein slope:

   $$h(t) = \frac{s}{T_e}\frac{(t/T_e)^{s-1}}{1 + (t/T_e)^s}\exp\left(\beta_8\,\mathrm{Dex} + \beta_9\,\mathrm{PCYTOMA} + \beta_{10} f(\mathrm{B2MG}) + \beta_{11}\frac{dM}{dt}\right)$$

# Population

The model was fitted to 201 patients with RRMM and measurable serum M-protein
from two single-agent isatuximab trials (Thai 2023 Tables 1-2): the
multinational phase II NCT01084252 (n = 170; 3 mg/kg q2w to 20 mg/kg qw-q2w,
38 of them with weekly dexamethasone 40 mg) and the Japanese phase I/II
NCT02812706 (n = 31; 10 or 20 mg/kg qw-q2w). Median age was 66 years (range
37-84), 46.3% were women, and median weight was 70 kg. Race was 70.6% White,
6.0% Black, 15.9% Asian. The median baseline serum M-protein was 28.1 g/L,
albumin 35 g/L and beta-2-microglobulin 4.53 mg/L. IgG myeloma made up 69.2%
and 15.4% had plasmacytomas. The analysis used 1774 serum M-protein
observations (median 9 per patient).

```{r population}
str(rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Thai_2023_isatuximab"))$population)
```

# Simulation set-up

Isatuximab is given as 3-hour infusions on days 0, 7, 14 and 21, then every 14
days. Dexamethasone is 40 mg weekly (20 mg for patients aged 75 or older),
dosed into `depot_kpd`. Simulations run for 88 weeks with weekly M-protein
observations.

```{r helpers}
mod <- readModelDb("Thai_2023_isatuximab")
tmax <- 616
isa_days <- c(0, 7, 14, 21, seq(28, tmax, by = 14))
obs_days <- seq(0, tmax, by = 7)

# One subject's events. dex_stop = Inf gives dexamethasone throughout;
# dex_stop = NA gives no dexamethasone.
make_events <- function(id, wt, mgkg, age, dex_stop) {
  isa <- data.frame(id = id, time = isa_days, amt = mgkg * wt, cmt = "central",
                    evid = 1, rate = mgkg * wt / 0.125)
  obs <- data.frame(id = id, time = obs_days, amt = NA_real_, cmt = "mprotein",
                    evid = 0, rate = NA_real_)
  out <- rbind(isa, obs)
  if (!is.na(dex_stop)) {
    dex_days <- seq(0, tmax - 1, by = 7)
    dex_days <- dex_days[dex_days < dex_stop]
    dex <- data.frame(id = id, time = dex_days, amt = ifelse(age >= 75, 20, 40),
                      cmt = "depot_kpd", evid = 1, rate = 0)
    out <- rbind(out, dex)
  }
  # The PFS dexamethasone indicator is 1 while the patient is on dexamethasone.
  out$CONMED_DEXAMETHASONE <- as.integer(!is.na(dex_stop) & out$time < dex_stop)
  out[order(out$time, -out$evid), ]
}
```

# Typical-patient covariate effects (Figure S6)

Figure S6 of Thai 2023 shows the M-protein and PFS curves of a typical patient
on isatuximab 20 mg/kg qw-q2w, varying one covariate at a time. The typical
patient here has the Table 2 medians, IgG myeloma, no plasmacytoma, the
non-Japanese study, lenalidomide-refractory disease and no dexamethasone; the
two unreported centring values (ALKN, number of prior lines) are at their
references.

```{r typical}
typ_cov <- data.frame(WT = 70, B2M = 4.53, MM_NIGG = 0, ALB = 35, ALPR = 1,
  N_PRIOR_LINES = 4, REGION_JAPAN = 0, REFRACTORY_LEN = 1, MCPROT = 28.1,
  DIS_EMD = 0, FORM_ISA_P2F2 = 1, RACE_ASIAN = 0, SEXF = 0, AGE = 66)
scenarios <- list(
  "Typical"                  = list(),
  "Non-IgG MM"               = list(MM_NIGG = 1),
  "Not lenalidomide-refractory" = list(REFRACTORY_LEN = 0),
  "Albumin 25 g/L"           = list(ALB = 25),
  "Baseline M-protein 70 g/L" = list(MCPROT = 70),
  "Plasmacytoma"             = list(DIS_EMD = 1),
  "Dexamethasone"            = list(dex = TRUE)
)
typ <- bind_rows(lapply(names(scenarios), function(nm) {
  sc <- scenarios[[nm]]
  cv <- typ_cov
  for (v in setdiff(names(sc), "dex")) cv[[v]] <- sc[[v]]
  ev <- make_events(1, cv$WT, 20, cv$AGE, if (isTRUE(sc$dex)) Inf else NA)
  ev <- cbind(ev, cv[rep(1, nrow(ev)), ])
  s <- rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), ev, returnType = "data.frame")
  s$scenario <- nm
  s
}))
typ <- typ |> distinct(scenario, time, .keep_all = TRUE)

ggplot(typ, aes(time / 7, mprotein, colour = scenario)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Time (weeks)", y = "Serum M-protein (g/L)", colour = NULL,
       caption = "Replicates the M-protein panels of Figure S6 of Thai 2023.")
ggplot(typ, aes(time / 7, surv_pfs, colour = scenario)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Time (weeks)", y = "PFS probability", colour = NULL,
       caption = "Replicates the PFS panels of Figure S6 of Thai 2023.")
```

```{r typical-check}
typ_sum <- typ |>
  group_by(scenario) |>
  summarise(
    m_80wk = mprotein[time == 560],
    median_pfs_wk = time[which(surv_pfs <= 0.5)[1]] / 7,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(ratio_to_typical = m_80wk / m_80wk[scenario == "Typical"])
typ_sum |>
  dplyr::rename("Scenario" = scenario, "M-protein at 80 weeks (g/L)" = m_80wk,
                "Median PFS (weeks)" = median_pfs_wk,
                "M-protein ratio to typical" = ratio_to_typical) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

r <- setNames(typ_sum$ratio_to_typical, typ_sum$scenario)
stopifnot(
  # Figure S6: the not-refractory curve ends at about 65 g/L against about
  # 215 g/L (ratio ~0.30); the non-IgG curve at about 140 g/L (ratio ~0.65).
  # These are deterministic typical-value solves.
  r[["Not lenalidomide-refractory"]] > 0.2, r[["Not lenalidomide-refractory"]] < 0.4,
  r[["Non-IgG MM"]] > 0.5, r[["Non-IgG MM"]] < 0.75,
  # Figure S6: the typical PFS curve crosses 0.5 at roughly 30 weeks.
  typ_sum$median_pfs_wk[typ_sum$scenario == "Typical"] > 25,
  typ_sum$median_pfs_wk[typ_sum$scenario == "Typical"] < 36
)
```

The covariate contrasts match Figure S6 closely. The covariates on M0 (IgG
type, albumin, ALKN, prior lines, Japanese study) scale the whole M-protein
curve, because the ODE is linear in M. The non-IgG contrast is stronger than
exp(-0.255) = 0.775 because non-IgG myeloma also lowers isatuximab clearance in
the Fau 2020 PK layer. The typical curve itself regrows more slowly than
Figure S6 (about 150 g/L at 80 weeks against about 215 g/L; see Assumptions and
deviations).

# Virtual cohort

Two hundred virtual patients are drawn to resemble Table 2. Each regimen is
simulated in the same patients with the same random effects, so the arms
differ only by treatment.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2023)
n <- 200
rtrunc_lnorm <- function(n, med, sdlog, lo, hi) pmin(pmax(exp(rnorm(n, log(med), sdlog)), lo), hi)
cohort <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(n),
  WT = rtrunc_lnorm(n, 70, 0.2, 37.6, 153),
  AGE = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n, 66, 9), 37), 84),
  B2M = rtrunc_lnorm(n, 4.53, 0.6, 1.32, 19.5),
  ALB = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n, 35, 5), 18), 48),
  ALPR = rtrunc_lnorm(n, 1, 0.4, 0.2, 5),
  N_PRIOR_LINES = pmin(pmax(round(rtrunc_lnorm(n, 4, 0.45, 1, 11)), 1), 11),
  REGION_JAPAN = rbinom(n, 1, 31 / 201),
  REFRACTORY_LEN = rbinom(n, 1, 0.85),
  MCPROT = rtrunc_lnorm(n, 28.1, 0.6, 6, 84),
  MM_NIGG = rbinom(n, 1, 62 / 201),
  DIS_EMD = rbinom(n, 1, 0.154),
  SEXF = rbinom(n, 1, 0.463),
  FORM_ISA_P2F2 = 1
)
cohort$RACE_ASIAN <- cohort$REGION_JAPAN

arms <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm,                       ~mgkg, ~dex_stop,
  "Isa 10 mg/kg qw-q2w",      10,    NA,
  "Isa 20 mg/kg qw-q2w",      20,    NA,
  "Isa 20 mg/kg qw-q2w + Dex", 20,   Inf,
  "Isa 20 mg/kg + Dex 0-3M",  20,    84,
  "Isa 20 mg/kg + Dex 0-6M",  20,    168
)

sim_arm <- function(mgkg, dex_stop) {
  ev <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(n), function(i) {
    make_events(i, cohort$WT[i], mgkg, cohort$AGE[i], dex_stop)
  }))
  ev <- left_join(ev, select(cohort, -AGE), by = "id")
  rxode2::rxSetSeed(20231)
  rxSolve(mod, ev, returnType = "data.frame")
}
sims <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms)), function(k) {
  s <- sim_arm(arms$mgkg[k], arms$dex_stop[k])
  s$arm <- arms$arm[k]
  s
})) |>
  distinct(arm, id, time, .keep_all = TRUE)
```

## Change in serum M-protein at week 8 (Figures 2a and 3a)

```{r week8}
wk8 <- sims |>
  filter(time %in% c(0, 56)) |>
  select(arm, id, time, mprotein) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = time, values_from = mprotein, names_prefix = "t") |>
  mutate(pct_change = 100 * (t56 / t0 - 1)) |>
  left_join(select(cohort, id, REGION_JAPAN), by = "id")

wk8 |>
  filter(arm %in% arms$arm[1:3]) |>
  ggplot(aes(arm, pmin(pct_change, 100))) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-100, 100)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Change from baseline in serum M-protein at week 8 (%)",
       caption = "Replicates Figures 2a and 3a of Thai 2023 (all patients).")
```

## PFS (Figures 2b and 3c, Table 4)

The population PFS curve is the mean of the individual survival curves.

```{r pfs}
pfs <- sims |>
  group_by(arm, time) |>
  summarise(surv = mean(surv_pfs), .groups = "drop")

pfs |>
  filter(arm %in% arms$arm[1:3]) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 7, surv, colour = arm)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Time (weeks)", y = "PFS probability", colour = NULL,
       caption = "Replicates Figures 2b and 3c of Thai 2023 (all patients).")

median_pfs <- function(time, surv) time[which(surv <= 0.5)[1]] / 7
pfs_med <- pfs |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarise(median_pfs_wk = median_pfs(time, surv), .groups = "drop")
```

## Comparison with the published simulations

```{r compare}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm,                       ~pub_wk8, ~pub_pfs,
  "Isa 10 mg/kg qw-q2w",      -22,      19.3 - 2.4,
  "Isa 20 mg/kg qw-q2w",      -30,      19.3,
  "Isa 20 mg/kg qw-q2w + Dex", -54,     25.6,
  "Isa 20 mg/kg + Dex 0-3M",  NA,       20.9,
  "Isa 20 mg/kg + Dex 0-6M",  NA,       21.3
)
cmp <- wk8 |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarise(sim_wk8 = median(pct_change), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(pfs_med, by = "arm") |>
  left_join(published, by = "arm") |>
  mutate(arm = factor(arm, levels = arms$arm)) |>
  arrange(arm)
cmp |>
  dplyr::rename("Regimen (all patients)" = arm,
                "Week-8 M-protein change, simulated (median %)" = sim_wk8,
                "Week-8 M-protein change, Thai 2023 (median %)" = pub_wk8,
                "Median PFS, simulated (weeks)" = median_pfs_wk,
                "Median PFS, Thai 2023 (weeks)" = pub_pfs) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

Published values: week-8 changes from the Results text (Figures 2a and 3a);
median PFS from Table 4. The 10 mg/kg median PFS is the 20 mg/kg value minus
the reported 2.4-week gain.

```{r compare-check}
paired <- wk8 |>
  select(arm, id, pct_change) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = arm, values_from = pct_change)
pfs_of <- function(a) cmp$median_pfs_wk[cmp$arm == a]
stopifnot(
  # Structural: monotherapy median PFS near the published 19.3 weeks.
  abs(pfs_of("Isa 20 mg/kg qw-q2w") - 19.3) < 5,
  # Dexamethasone prolongs PFS, and full-duration dexamethasone more than
  # 3 months of it.
  pfs_of("Isa 20 mg/kg qw-q2w + Dex") > pfs_of("Isa 20 mg/kg qw-q2w"),
  pfs_of("Isa 20 mg/kg qw-q2w + Dex") >= pfs_of("Isa 20 mg/kg + Dex 0-3M"),
  # Paired within patient (same random effects): the higher dose and the
  # added dexamethasone lower week-8 M-protein for the median patient.
  median(paired[["Isa 20 mg/kg qw-q2w"]] - paired[["Isa 10 mg/kg qw-q2w"]]) < 0,
  median(paired[["Isa 20 mg/kg qw-q2w + Dex"]] - paired[["Isa 20 mg/kg qw-q2w"]]) < 0
)
```

Median PFS is close to Table 4 for isatuximab 20 mg/kg alone (about 20
against 19.3 weeks) and with dexamethasone (about 27 against 25.6 weeks), and
the week-8 decrease with dexamethasone is close to the published 54%. The
week-8 decrease on isatuximab alone is smaller than published (about 18%
against 30% at 20 mg/kg, and about 4% against 22% at 10 mg/kg), and the
short-duration dexamethasone arms keep more of the full-duration PFS gain than
Table 4 reports. The virtual cohort draws covariates that the paper does not
report (lenalidomide-refractory fraction, number of prior lines, ALKN), uses
population rather than individual PK, and reads the between-subject
variability as Monolix standard deviations (see Assumptions and deviations),
so these centres can move by several percentage points or weeks.

## Japanese patients (Figure 3b and 3d)

```{r japanese}
wk8 |>
  filter(REGION_JAPAN == 1, arm %in% arms$arm[2:3]) |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarise(n = n(), median_wk8_change = median(pct_change), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::rename("Regimen (Japanese patients)" = arm, "N" = n,
                "Week-8 M-protein change (median %)" = median_wk8_change) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

Thai 2023 reports medians of -43% (isatuximab alone) and -67% (with
dexamethasone) in Japanese patients. The virtual Japanese subgroup shows a smaller
decrease on isatuximab alone (about -32%) and a similar one with dexamethasone
(about -62%); with about 30 Japanese patients these medians are imprecise.

# Isatuximab exposure (PKNCA)

Thai 2023 reports no NCA. As a check on the embedded PK layer, PKNCA computes
the first-week Cmax and AUC of the typical patient at each dose.

```{r pknca}
nca_typ <- bind_rows(lapply(c(10, 20), function(d) {
  ev <- et(amt = d * 70, time = 0, cmt = "central", rate = d * 70 / 0.125) |>
    et(seq(0, 7, by = 0.125), cmt = "central")
  ev <- cbind(as.data.frame(ev), typ_cov[rep(1, nrow(as.data.frame(ev))), ])
  ev$CONMED_DEXAMETHASONE <- 0
  s <- rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), ev, returnType = "data.frame")
  s$treatment <- paste(d, "mg/kg")
  s$id <- 1
  s
}))
conc <- nca_typ |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  distinct(treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  select(id, treatment, time, Cc)
dose <- data.frame(id = 1, treatment = c("10 mg/kg", "20 mg/kg"), time = 0,
                   amt = c(700, 1400))
pc <- PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
pd <- PKNCAdose(dose, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 7, cmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca <- pk.nca(PKNCAdata(pc, pd, intervals = intervals))
nca_tab <- as.data.frame(nca$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "auclast")) |>
  select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)
nca_tab |>
  dplyr::rename("Dose" = treatment, "Cmax (mg/L)" = cmax,
                "AUC0-7 days (mg*day/L)" = auclast) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
# Doubling the dose roughly doubles first-week exposure (linear CL dominates
# at these concentrations, far above the 0.3 mg/L Michaelis-Menten Km).
stopifnot(abs(nca_tab$auclast[2] / nca_tab$auclast[1] - 2) < 0.15)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Covariate form.** The paper prints no covariate equations. Monolix
  log-normal parameters with continuous covariates are encoded as
  `log(P) = log(Ppop) + beta * log(cov / reference)`. Figure S6 supports this:
  a linear MPROT term of -0.56 per g/L would remove almost all drug effect at
  high baseline M-protein, and the albumin P5 curve starts near 50 g/L, which
  matches (25/35)^-1.83 = 1.85 times 27 g/L. References are the Table 2
  medians (albumin 35 g/L, baseline M-protein 28.1 g/L, B2M 4.53 mg/L).
  Albumin normalised to the upper limit of normal (ALBN) is entered as
  absolute albumin, since the ULN cancels in the ratio to the median.
* **Unreported centring values.** The medians of ALKN (alkaline phosphatase /
  ULN) and of the number of prior lines are not reported. The model centres
  ALKN on the ULN (`ALPR = 1`) and prior lines on 4. A typical patient whose
  true medians differ two-fold would have M0 off by about 17%.
* **New covariate columns.** The maintainers registered `ALPR` (alkaline
  phosphatase / ULN), `N_PRIOR_LINES` (continuous count of prior lines) and
  `REFRACTORY_LEN` (1 = lenalidomide-refractory). The paper's effect is on
  'REF_Len = N', so the model applies it as `(1 - REFRACTORY_LEN)`.
* **Between-subject variability.** Monolix reports omega as the standard
  deviation of the random effect; Table 3's 'Interindividual variability (%)'
  is read as 100 * omega and squared (for example 1.23^2 = 1.51 for EC50). If
  the column were instead a CV, the variances would be log(1 + CV^2) (0.92 for
  EC50). Only the spread of individual curves depends on this choice, not the
  typical values. In the virtual cohort the CV reading moved the monotherapy
  week-8 median from about -18% to about -25% and the median PFS by about 2
  weeks, so the published simulations do not settle it.
* **Residual error.** Monolix's default combined error model `a + b*f` is
  encoded with `combined1()`.
* **Isatuximab PK.** Thai 2023 drove the model with individual post-hoc PK
  parameters (typical values for 4 patients without PK). Here the Fau 2020
  population model is embedded with its covariates and variability fixed. The
  Japanese trial was later found to have lower isatuximab clearance in a
  pooled PK analysis that is not reproduced here, so the Japanese-patient
  simulations use the Fau 2020 covariates only (Asian race on Vc).
* **Convention check.** `checkModelConventions()` warns that `cl_time_max`
  is not log-transformed. It is carried over unchanged from
  `Fau_2020_isatuximab`: CLm is a signed log-ratio with a normally
  distributed random effect, so a log transform would not fit.
* **Hazard start time.** The Monolix code switches the hazard on at a
  per-patient time `Tstart`, whose values are not given. The hazard here runs
  from the first dose.
* **Numerical cap on the hazard.** The log of the hazard multiplier is capped
  at 50. When simulated M-protein regrows at several g/L per day,
  `6.65 * dM/dt` overflows `exp()`; at the cap, survival is already zero, so
  the cap only prevents `Inf`/`NaN` values.
* **B2M effect on PFS.** beta10 = -1.76e-7 is negligible under either a log or
  a linear covariate form (Thai 2023 describe it as "extremely low"). It is
  encoded as `log(B2M / 4.53)` for consistency.
* **Dexamethasone indicator.** The PFS covariate 'Dex = Y' is the randomised
  arm. In the short-duration scenarios it is switched off when dexamethasone
  stops; the paper does not say how it handled this.
* **Typical curve versus Figure S6.** The typical patient's M-protein falls to
  about 16 g/L at week 11 and reaches about 150 g/L at week 80, whereas
  Figure S6 shows a shallower nadir and about 215 g/L. The covariate contrasts
  and the typical median PFS (about 30 weeks) match the figure. The cause of
  the gap was not found; the figure's typical patient may use different PK or
  covariate values from those assumed here.
* **Table 2 typo.** The 'All' column prints 31 (15.4%) non-IgG patients, a copy
  of the plasmacytoma row; the per-trial counts (56 + 6 = 62, 30.8%) are used.
* **Virtual-cohort covariates not reported in the paper.** The
  lenalidomide-refractory fraction (85%), the spread of ALKN and prior lines,
  and age are assumptions. Infusion duration (3 hours) is also assumed.
* No erratum to Thai 2023 was found (checked 2026-11-07).
